Okay, so I'm trying to figure out in which century Tecumseh became the primary leader of a large, multi-tribal confederacy. I know that Tecumseh was a Shawnee chief and that his brother, Tenskwatawa, was involved in the Tippecanoe order of battle. I remember that Tecumseh was active in the early 19th century, but I'm not exactly sure about the specific century.

First, I think about the time period. Tecumseh lived from 1768 to 1813, so he was around during the late 18th and early 19th centuries. His brother Tenskwatawa was known as the Prophet and was involved in forming the confederacy. I believe that Tecumseh started leading this confederacy around the early 1800s, maybe around 1808 or so.

I recall that the confederacy was formed to resist white encroachment and that Tecumseh traveled widely to unite various tribes. He joined the British during the War of 1812, which was in the early 1800s. His death in 1813 marked the end of his leadership, so his confederacy must have been active until then.

I'm a bit confused about whether this is the 18th or 19th century. Since the confederacy was formed in the early 1800s, it's definitely the 19th century. I think the key here is to confirm the exact start year, but from what I gather, it's around 1808, which is within the 19th century.

So, putting it all together, Tecumseh became the primary leader of the confederacy in the 19th century, specifically around 1808.
